newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Social affairs ministers to debate unemployment.
newsitem.headline: Social affairs ministers to debate unemployment.

text.p: European Union social affairs and employment ministers will debate ways to coordinate efforts to bring down unemployment at an informal meeting on Friday and Saturday in Rotterdam.
At Belgium's request, they will also discuss the recent decision by French carmaker Renault to close a plant in Belgium, EU officials said.
During the unemployment debate, the ministers will look especially at the question of tax policies that may be hampering job creation and at the use of common economic indicators, EU officials said.

"Taxation systems should be made more employment-friendly by ensuring that they provide clear incentives for job seekers to take jobs and for employers to hire more workers," a paper prepared by the Dutch presidency says.

It notes that charges on capital are falling in Europe while those on labour are rising and says the Social Affairs Council could give debate over that problem "fresh momentum". Up to now, it says, the issue has been discussed only by the ECOFIN Council.
The ministers will also discuss ways to develop common employment indicators in the member states so the EU can monitor labour-market developments and determine which policies are most effective.

The indicators should measure the outcome of various policies, such as those aimed at fighting general unemployment along with those targeted as priority areas such as young people, women and the long-term unemployed, the paper says.
They should also look at issues such as investment in vocational training and reducing non-wage labour costs, it says.

The paper says the EU needs to coordinate employment policies as it builds a monetary union. "A stable, competitive currency has to bring with it a common social and economic policy, social stability being a necessary condition for economic integration," it says.
In addition to their discussions, the ministers will participate in a European Youth Forum on Friday afternoon and visit some employment projects in Rotterdam on Saturday.
